name: Greyish brownish olive
lede: Greyish brownish olive is a muted, dark khaki, the library's double-modified variant of plain [[olive]], and it is one of the more common named colors in our archive.

sections.title: A modifier on an existing name
sections.body: The library stacks two modifiers at once on the base entry [[olive]], filing "greyish brownish" as a single combined variant alongside siblings such as [[pale-olive]], [[deep-olive]] and [[olive-brown]] [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same patch as olive gray, only 2.2 units away in CIEDE2000, the closest match of any color, and Ridgway's 1912 atlas lists a corresponding block too [1]. Measured in LCH it has lightness 37, chroma 9 and hue 97 degrees, and [[gunmetal]] than to a bright olive [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive, a match appears in 2,887 of 23,781 paintings, about 12.1 percent, as photographed, making it one of the most frequent named colors we track; the within-painting lens finds it in 1,761 [2]. That is ahead of 94 percent of our named colors [2]. It most often plays a mid-tone, in 30 percent of its appearances [2]. It peaks in the 1100s, in 6 of 50 paintings, 12.0 percent of the 50 paintings (6 of them) we have from that century, about 1.2 times the archive's typical rate, though that century is thinly represented in the archive [2]. Philips Wouwerman is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 11 of his 36 archived works, 3.7 times the typical rate [2]. It shares canvases more than chance would predict with [[mouse-grey]] and [[cannon]] [2].

issues: Field notes named the wrong painter and stat (claimed Dirck van Delen, 8/13; real fieldnotes data show Philips Wouwerman, 11/36, 3.7x), a wrong painting count/role breakdown (claimed 4,196 paintings and 'shadows close behind at 30%'; real is 2,887/17.6%, shadow is 17% not 30%), a fabricated 'Tibetan paintings' claim with no supporting country data, and the wrong companion colors; corrected to the real counts, painter, role and companions.
